{{Short description|Topic in abstract algebra}}
In [[abstract algebra]], a '''[[semigroup]] with three elements''' is an object consisting of three elements and an [[associative operation]] defined on them. The basic example would be the three integers 0, 1, and −1, together with the operation of multiplication. Multiplication of integers is associative, and the product of any two of these three integers is again one of these three integers.

There are 18 inequivalent ways to define an associative operation on three elements: while there are, altogether, a total of 3<sup>9</sup> = 19683 different binary operations that can be defined, only 113 of these are associative, and many of these are [[isomorphic]] or [[antiisomorphic]] so that there are essentially only 18 possibilities.<ref name=distler>Andreas Distler, [http://bcc2009.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Theses/andreasDthesis.pdf Classification and enumeration of finite semigroups] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402121217/http://bcc2009.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Theses/andreasDthesis.pdf |date=2015-04-02 }}, PhD thesis, [[University of St. Andrews]].  See also [https://docs.gap-system.org/pkg/smallsemi/doc/chap0_mj.html].</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Friðrik Diego|author2=Kristín Halla Jónsdóttir |title=Associative Operations on a Three-Element Set|journal=The Montana Mathematics Enthusiast|date=July 2008|volume=5|issue=2 & 3|pages=257–268|doi=10.54870/1551-3440.1106 |s2cid=118704099 |url=http://www.math.umt.edu/tmme/vol5no2and3/TMME_vol5nos2and3_a8_pp.257_268.pdf|accessdate=6 February 2014}}</ref>

One of these is C<sub>3</sub>, the [[cyclic group]] with three elements. The others all have a [[semigroup with two elements]] as [[subsemigroup]]s. In the example above, the set {−1,0,1} under multiplication contains both {0,1} and {−1,1} as subsemigroups (the latter is a sub''group'', [[cyclic group|C<sub>2</sub>]]). 

Six of these are [[band (mathematics)|bands]], meaning that all three elements are [[idempotent]], so that the product of any element with itself is itself again. Two of these bands are [[commutative]], therefore [[semilattices]] (one of them is the three-element totally ordered set, and the other is a three-element semilattice that is not a lattice). The other four come in anti-isomorphic pairs. 

One of these non-commutative bands results from adjoining an [[identity element]] to LO<sub>2</sub>, the [[left zero semigroup]] with two elements (or, dually, to RO<sub>2</sub>, the [[right zero semigroup]]). It is sometimes called the '''flip-flop monoid''', referring to [[flip-flop (electronics)|flip-flop circuits]] used in electronics: the three elements can be described as "set", "reset", and "do nothing". This semigroup occurs in the [[Krohn–Rhodes theory|Krohn–Rhodes decomposition]] of finite semigroups.<ref>"This innocuous three-element semigroup plays an important role in what follows..." – [https://books.google.com/books?id=0ukzw5VszNwC Applications of Automata Theory and Algebra] by [[John Rhodes (mathematician)|John L. Rhodes]].</ref> The irreducible elements in this decomposition are the [[finite simple groups]] plus this three-element semigroup, and its subsemigroups.

There are two [[cyclic semigroup]]s, one described by the equation ''x''<sup>4</sup> = ''x''<sup>3</sup>, which has O<sub>2</sub>, the [[null semigroup]] with two elements, as a subsemigroup. The other is described by ''x''<sup>4</sup> = ''x''<sup>2</sup> and has C<sub>2</sub>, the group with two elements, as a subgroup. (The equation ''x''<sup>4</sup> = ''x'' describes C<sub>3</sub>, the group with three elements, already mentioned.)

There are seven other non-cyclic non-band commutative semigroups, including the initial example of {−1, 0, 1}, and O<sub>3</sub>, the null semigroup with three elements. There are also two other anti-isomorphic pairs of non-commutative non-band semigroups.
